title: SparrowBench — sessionized throughput vs amortized spend (vignette)
content:
Purpose:
This vignette is a compact, informal record of a small internal benchmark we ran to explore how sessionized workloads (many short conversations) change the trade-offs between latency SLOs and amortized spend. It is intentionally short — working notes + a couple of ascii charts so we can decide whether to schedule a deeper sweep.

Quick TL;DR:
- For low-token interactive sessions (median 12 tokens per response), keeping warm session affinity reduces amortized spend by ~35% at p99 targets compared to fully cold requests, while improving p50 latency by ~10ms.
- For long-form single-shot generation (median 1,200 tokens), amortized spend is dominated by token compute; session warmup has negligible dollar impact but can shave tail latency for the first chunk.
- Mixed workloads (50/50 split) show nonlinear effects: small reductions in cache hitrate cause p99 to jump and cost to increase more than linear interpolation predicts.

Test setup (short):
- Model: open-llama-34b-8k-quant (representative open model)
- Hardware: dedicated A100-sim node (single-GPU profile used for comparability)
- Runtime: local runner with dynamic batching disabled for the micro-run; KV cache enabled where session affinity set
- Workload generator: synthetic sessionizer that produces N sessions/min with per-session turn distributions sampled from a small seed trace (internal customer simulation).
- Measured: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) for response generation, tokens generated per request, cost estimate (dollars) per 1k tokens using our internal cost-per-token model, and amortized cost per session (dollars/session).

Scenarios (keys):
A) Interactive short-turns (IS): 300 sessions/min, median turns per session = 8, median tokens/turn = 12
B) Long-shot generation (LG): 50 sessions/min, single request per session, median tokens = 1,200
C) Mixed (MX): 150 sessions/min, mix 50% IS / 50% LG by count

Representative numbers (approx, anonymized):
- Cost unit: $0.000012 per token (inference compute + amortized infra) — internal model for this run

Scenario A (IS):
- p50 latency: 78 ms (warm affinity) vs 88 ms (no affinity)
- p90 latency: 143 ms vs 210 ms
- p99 latency: 356 ms vs 820 ms
- tokens/request: 12
- requests/session (per conversation): 8 turns => ~96 tokens/session
- cost/session: 96 * $0.000012 = $0.001152 (warm) vs $0.00176 (cold) => ~35% savings

Scenario B (LG):
- p50 latency: 1,240 ms vs 1,310 ms
- p90 latency: 1,430 ms vs 1,520 ms
- p99 latency: 2,100 ms vs 2,170 ms
- tokens/request: 1,200
- cost/session: 1,200 * $0.000012 = $0.0144 (warm) vs $0.01464 (cold) => ~1.7% savings (negligible)

Scenario C (MX):
- Aggregate p99 (observed): 780 ms (with affinity) vs 1,250 ms (no affinity)
- tokens-weighted cost per session: 0.5 * 0.001152 + 0.5 * 0.0144 = 0.007776 (warm) vs 0.5 * 0.00176 + 0.5 * 0.01464 = 0.0082 (no affinity) => ~5% savings overall
- BUT: when KV cache hitrate drops from 92% -> 78% in the mixed run (simulated noisy routing), p99 rises by +420 ms and cost per session increases by ~9% relative to the high-hitrate case.

Ascii visualizations (simple):

- IS warm: ▇▇▇▇ (356)
- IS cold: ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (820)
- LG warm: ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (2100)
- LG cold: ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (2170)
- MX warm: ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (780)
- MX cold: ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (1250)

2) cost per session ($) — values and relative markers (each * ~ $0.002):
- IS warm: $0.00115  (*)
- IS cold: $0.00176  (**)
- LG warm: $0.01440  (***********)
- LG cold: $0.01464  (************)
- MX warm: $0.00778  (******)
- MX cold: $0.00820  (*******)

Observations / Interpretations (working):
- Small per-request token counts make session-level state (cache + warm workers) a lever both for tail latency and for cost: the overhead of model startup and rehydrating KV cache dominates the per-turn cost. We should think of interactive workflows as "tail-latency sensitive and cache-sensitive" rather than token-cost sensitive.
- Long-shot work is token-cost driven; micro-optimizations to keep a worker warm have diminishing dollar returns but still matter for tail smoothing on the first chunk.
- Mixed traffic is the hard case: if affinity policies occasionally misroute or cache hitrate stutters, p99 sensitivity amplifies and creates a disproportionate cost/latency penalty.

Open questions / next steps (practical):
- Sweep idea: run a fuller matrix across 3 models (small/med/large), 3 hardware tiers, and varying affinity TTLs to quantify the break-even points for reserved warmers.
- Dev ops ask: can we instrument a simple KV-hit metric at the route level for a 2-week pilot to validate the synthetic hitrate assumptions? (JIRA:INF-1892)
- Product: define a recommended default affinity TTL for interactive endpoints (current guess: 60s) and measure impact on billing flows and SLA notifications.
- UX: warn customers in console when session patterns indicate >20% tail sensitivity (prototype alert we sketched in PR 492).

Notes to self (rough):
- This doc is intentionally short and anecdotal. Bring it up in next Console standup (Mon) and propose a formal sweep with Platform.
- Keep the raw logs around for one month (we tagged them with INF-1876-run-20280728).

Appendix (data caveats):
- Numbers rounded, internal cost model used for $/token is illustrative only. Keep assumptions in sync with Finance if we plan to publish externally.
- Load generator was deterministic for reproducibility but not fully representative of real-world jitter; expect p99 to vary in the wild.

Action items (owner tags):
- Aisha: schedule sweep proposal and draft the experiment matrix (due 2028-08-04)
- Marco: add KV-hit instrumentation to the route metrics prototype (JIRA:INF-1892)
- Sofia: check cost-per-token assumptions against FinOps (put on FYI deck)

End of vignette.
